column2: How do I send the photos from my phone to the computer over wifi?
column3: On the computer: Settings → 🖧 Several computers (door open, password set) → “＋ Add a field phone”: scan the QR code with the phone, compare the 6-digit code on both screens and allow it as a “📱 Field phone”. The phone’s page opens in its browser, with nothing to install: give the family tree’s password (asked again after 15 minutes without activity), then 📷 Take or 🖼 Choose, a line of text, “Who is it for?” (optional), ⤒ Send. The photos arrive in Lists → Media and documents → 📥 To sort, outside the tree: “🔗 Link” each one to a person, an event, a source or the visit, or 🗑 Delete it (kept 30 days), always with “↶ Undo”. The GPS position is removed on arrival (a setting). The phone never sees the tree: for “Who is it for?” it only sees archive visits and deceased people. As with the other computers, what goes over the wifi isn’t encrypted: only use your home wifi, protected by its key.

column2: And without wifi, at the cemetery or the town hall?
column3: Open the phone’s page before you leave and don’t close the tab: photos taken without the home wifi wait in the page (in the phone’s browser) and go off by themselves when it finds the wifi again, with a new try every 30 seconds. The page can’t open away from the wifi: that would need a “service worker”, which browsers only allow with HTTPS, and the wifi door has none. The phone can also erase waiting photos if it runs out of space (Safari does so after a few days): rather take the photos with the phone’s camera, then “🖼 Choose” when you’re back. For a whole day at the archives, the visit by file (a .html page taken along, then a .zip brought back) is still there.
